lines.japanese: ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー……。
lines.english: Coo-coo, coo-coo, coo-coo…

lines.japanese: 眠りの向こうで無機質なさえずりが響いていた。
lines.english: Beyond the veil of sleep, a mechanical birdcall rang out.

lines.japanese: 目覚まし時計が鳴っている、みたいだ。
lines.english: It sounded like my alarm clock.

lines.japanese: 僕はまぶたを開くより先に腕を伸ばして、騒音の発信源を探りあてた。そのてっぺんのアラーム停止ボタンを、叩くように押す。
lines.english: Before I even opened my eyes, I reached out and felt around until I found the source of the noise. I slapped the alarm button on top.

lines.japanese: ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー……。
lines.english: Coo-coo, coo-coo, coo-coo…

lines.japanese: しかし状況は変わらない。
lines.english: Nothing changed.

lines.japanese: おかしい。どうして止まってくれないんだろう。わけが分からないまま、僕は目をこじ開けてのっそり敷き布団の上に立ちあがった。
lines.english: Strange. Why would it not stop? Mystified, I pried my eyes open and hauled myself to my feet on the bedding.

lines.japanese: 心地よい繭から抜けでた１２月の朝はひどい寒さで、眠気がたちどころに吹きとぶようだった。
lines.english: Outside the warm cocoon of my blankets, the December morning was brutally cold—enough, it seemed, to banish sleep in an instant.

lines.japanese: 吹きとばないけど。
lines.english: It did not.

lines.japanese: 僕は足元を見下ろした。枕の横にいつものアラームクロックが「おとなしく」転がっていた。
lines.english: I looked down. My usual alarm clock lay beside my pillow, perfectly “quiet.”

lines.japanese: あれ、違う、これじゃない。いつまでも融通の利かない騒音は、枕元ではなく部屋の外から鳴りひびいていた。
lines.english: Oh. Wrong one. The noise, stubbornly indifferent to my wishes, was coming from outside the room rather than beside my pillow.

lines.japanese: 僕は起きぬけのなまった体を引きずって歩いた。
lines.english: I dragged my sluggish, newly wakened body toward it.

lines.japanese: ふすまを開ける。
lines.english: I opened the sliding door.

lines.japanese: 光沢のある板目の上で、鳥の巣箱をモチーフにした小さな置き時計がひたすら事務的にさえずっていた。
lines.english: On the glossy woodgrain floor, a little clock shaped like a birdhouse was chirping away with tireless efficiency.

lines.japanese: ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー、ぽっぽー……。
lines.english: Coo-coo, coo-coo, coo-coo…

lines.japanese: 僕は崩れおちるようにしゃがみこんでそれを拾う。
lines.english: I folded to a crouch and picked it up.

lines.japanese: 「……おはよ」
lines.english: “…Morning.”

lines.japanese: 裏側のスイッチをＯＦＦにしてから、文字盤の中央よりすこし上に描かれた元気なハトさんと朝の挨拶を交わした。
lines.english: After switching it off at the back, I exchanged morning greetings with the cheerful little pigeon painted just above the center of the clock face.

lines.japanese: 長針を見れば、いつも起きている時刻を１０分ほど過ぎている。
lines.english: The minute hand told me I was already ten minutes past my usual waking time.

lines.japanese: ……なるほど。どうやら僕はゆうべ、自分の目覚まし時計をセットしないまま眠ってしまったらしい。
lines.english: …I see. Apparently I had gone to sleep last night without setting my alarm.

lines.japanese: ひとつの光景を想像する。兄の時計が定時になっても鳴らないので、部屋の外にそっと（あるいはドンッと）自分の目覚ましを置いていく妹。
lines.english: I pictured the scene: her brother’s clock fails to ring at the appointed hour, so his little sister quietly sets her own outside his room—or perhaps puts it down with a bang.

lines.japanese: そのとき彼女がどんな表情をしていたかによって意味合いは変わってくるわけだけど、僕は好意的に解釈して、それでじゅうぶん微笑ましい気分になる。ことにした。
lines.english: The meaning would change depending on the expression she wore at the time, of course. I chose the charitable interpretation and allowed it to warm my heart. Or decided that it did.

lines.japanese: どのみち「おにいちゃん朝だよ～」なんて言って起こしてくれる妹は、画面の向こう側にしか存在しないんだ。
lines.english: In any case, little sisters who came in singing, ‘Rise and shine, sleepyhead!’ existed only on the other side of a screen.

lines.japanese: 「それにしても……」
lines.english: “Still…”

lines.japanese: 部屋に戻ってカーテンを開けると、紛うことなき月曜の朝がそこにあった。
lines.english: I went back into my room and opened the curtains. An unmistakable Monday morning waited beyond them.

lines.japanese: 窓の外、白く霞んだような冬の住宅街から、作り物の鳩さんとは違う遠慮がちなさえずりが聞こえる。
lines.english: Outside the window, from the winter neighborhood washed in a whitish haze, came a timid birdsong quite unlike the clockwork pigeon’s.

lines.japanese: 「また……負けちゃったのか……」
lines.english: “I lost again…”

lines.japanese: 睡魔に。
lines.english: To sleep.

lines.japanese: まだ拭いきれない眠気もあって、僕は遮光カーテンを掴んだまま、冬の窓辺でしばし放心してしまった。
lines.english: Still not entirely free of it, I stood at the wintry window with the blackout curtain in my hand and drifted blankly for a while.

lines.japanese: 広げられたままの数学ノートに目を落とせば、シャーペンの文字がグラフの上で、壊れたエアプレーンみたいにふらふら踊っていた。
lines.english: I lowered my eyes to the open math notebook. Across the graph, my mechanical-pencil marks reeled and danced like a damaged airplane.

lines.japanese: ノートをめくり、飛行記録をさかのぼってみる。たしかに途中までは勤勉な航行だった。
lines.english: I turned back through the notebook, retracing the flight. For a while, at least, it had been a diligent, orderly voyage.

lines.japanese: そう、途中までは。
lines.english: For a while.

lines.japanese: その後に続く、ぐにゃぐにゃと踊った文字とも呼べない線は、すさまじい眠気との格闘を思わせる壮絶な筆記だ。
lines.english: Then came the wild, writhing lines that could no longer be called letters: a harrowing written record of my battle against overwhelming sleep.

lines.japanese: 僕はノートをそっと閉じる。今日のテストは負け戦だ。
lines.english: I gently closed the notebook. Today’s exam was already a lost battle.

lines.japanese: 「はあー……」
lines.english: “Haaaah…”
“…Aaahh.”

lines.japanese: 自己嫌悪に肩を落としたら、絶望の溜息さえあくびになって返ってきた。
lines.english: My shoulders sagged with self-disgust, and even my despairing sigh came back as a yawn.

lines.japanese: まあ、７０点ぐらいならなんとかなる……かな。
lines.english: Well, I could probably manage something like a seventy… probably.

lines.japanese: 気が重いまま制服に着替え、一階へ下りた。
lines.english: Heavy at heart, I changed into my uniform and went downstairs.

lines.japanese: 廊下から覗いた居間には、もそもそと静かにトーストをかじる制服の小鳩と、画面の中で朝のニュースを読みあげるスーツ姿のアナウンサーがいた。
lines.english: Peering into the living room from the hall, I found Kobato in her uniform, quietly nibbling at a piece of toast, and a suited announcer inside the television reading the morning news.

lines.japanese: 脚の低い座卓を見る。白い皿の上に載った食パンと、マグカップの中のインスタントスープ。粗食のきわみだ。叔母さんがいない朝の食卓は、殺風景でとても広く感じられる。
lines.english: I looked at the low table: sliced bread on a white plate, instant soup in a mug. Spartan fare at its finest. Without my aunt, the breakfast table looked bare and felt terribly large.

lines.japanese: 兄妹ふたりだけの朝餉は、羽田家では滅多にないシチュエーション。僕は“妹と毎日会話をする”という課題を思いだしてすこし気を張り、ついでに声の方も張ってみた。
lines.english: A morning meal alone with my sister was a rare situation in the Haneda household. Remembering my assignment to “speak with my sister every day,” I braced myself and put a little extra strength into my voice.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう。目覚ましありがとう、助かったよ」
lines.english: “Good morning. Thanks for the alarm. You saved me.”

lines.japanese: 居間の畳を踏みしめながら、台本の台詞を読みあげるみたいに言った。
lines.english: I said it as I stepped onto the tatami, sounding as though I were reading a line from a script.

lines.japanese: 「んっ？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は朝のニュースから目を転じて、はっと僕を見上げた。両手で持ったトーストを千切らずに直接かぶりついている様子が、齧歯目の小動物みたいだった。
lines.english: Kobato tore her eyes from the morning news and looked up at me with a start. She held the toast in both hands and bit directly into it instead of tearing off pieces, like some tiny rodent.

lines.japanese: 「あ……おは、おはよ」
lines.english: “Oh… G-good morning.”

lines.japanese: しかし彼女は朝の最低限の挨拶を返すと、食べかけのパンを皿に戻して慌ただしく立ちあがった。
lines.english: But once she had returned the bare minimum of a morning greeting, she set her half-eaten toast on its plate and scrambled to her feet.

lines.japanese: そして目も合わせずに僕の前を通りすぎ、扉のない入り口をくぐってダイニングへと姿を消した。
lines.english: Without meeting my eyes, she hurried past me, through the open doorway, and disappeared into the dining room.
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 僕はその行方を見送ったまま立ちつくす。
lines.english: I stood rooted to the spot, staring after her.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。
lines.english: What was that about?

lines.japanese: むかし……僕が朝の挨拶を投げたとき、そうやって遠ざかっていった磯村さんの真っ赤なランドセルを思いだした。
lines.english: It reminded me of long ago… of Isomura’s bright red schoolbag receding in just that way after I called good morning to her.

lines.japanese: 思えばあの頃ぐらいから僕は、女性という生き物と話すのが苦手になったのかもしれない。だから髪を切ってもらうときも、男性美容師の多い店へ通うようにしている。
lines.english: Perhaps that was when I first lost my knack for speaking to the female of the species. Even now, whenever I needed a haircut, I made a point of going somewhere with plenty of male stylists.

lines.japanese: 「何枚？」
lines.english: “How many?”

lines.japanese: 居間のとば口で突っ立っていると、不意に戸棚の陰から声がした。
lines.english: As I stood there in the living-room entrance, her voice suddenly came from behind the cupboards.
“What?”

lines.japanese: 僕は首を伸ばしてダイニングを覗きこんだ。キッチンテーブルの端に立った小鳩が、オーブントースターに食パンをセットしようとしていた。
lines.english: I craned my neck into the dining room. Kobato stood at one end of the kitchen table, about to put bread into the toaster oven.

lines.japanese: 「あ……た、食べない？」
lines.english: “Oh… A-aren’t you eating?”
“What? No, I…”

lines.japanese: どうやら僕の分を焼いてくれるみたいだ。
lines.english: Apparently she meant to make some for me.

lines.japanese: 今日は朝食の時間さえ惜しんで、教室でテスト開始ぎりぎりまで教科書を読んでいようと思っていた。だけど僕は予定を変更した。
lines.english: I had planned to skip breakfast and spend every last moment before the exam reading my textbook in the classroom. I changed my plans.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、一枚おねがい」
lines.english: “Then one slice, please.”

lines.japanese: 人差し指を立てて明るく告げる。返事はなかったけど、すぐにオーブンの蓋を閉じる音が聞こえた。
lines.english: I raised one finger and said it brightly. She did not answer, but a moment later I heard the toaster oven click shut.

lines.japanese: 僕がそのまま宿題を忘れた小学生みたいに立っていると、小鳩がコンロに火を点けてから振りかえった。
lines.english: I remained where I was, looking like a grade-schooler who had forgotten his homework. After lighting the stove, Kobato turned around.

lines.japanese: 「あ……座っ、座ってていいよ」
lines.english: “You… You can sit down.”

lines.japanese: 聞きとりにくい声。
lines.english: Her voice was scarcely audible.
“You sure…?”

lines.japanese: 見られていると落ちつかないのかもしれない。僕は小鳩が座っていた席の対面にそろそろと腰を落とした。
lines.english: Perhaps she could not settle down with me watching. I gingerly lowered myself into the place across from where she had been sitting.

lines.japanese: しかし何もせずにただ待っている方だって、同じくらい落ちつかない。僕の肩は無意識のうちにすぼまっていた。
lines.english: But sitting there doing nothing was just as uncomfortable. Before I knew it, my shoulders had drawn inward.

lines.japanese: つけっぱなしのテレビ画面に映ってゆくのは、どこかの街の暴力団事務所。報道陣の待つ警察署前。押収されたトカレフ型拳銃。画面左上に「資料映像」と白いテロップ。
lines.english: The television, still playing unattended, showed a gang’s offices in some city. Reporters waiting outside a police station. A confiscated Tokarev-style pistol. In the upper left, a white caption read FILE FOOTAGE.

lines.japanese: 公共放送の男性キャスターが読みあげる低音の銃殺事件は、なんだか兄妹の朝の食卓をより窮屈にさせる気がした。
lines.english: The public broadcaster’s male anchor recited the details of a fatal shooting in a low voice. Somehow, it made the morning table around my sister and me feel smaller still.

lines.japanese: しばらく見るともなしに眺めていたけど、けっきょく僕はテーブルの上に載っていたリモコンのボタンを、拾いあげずに指先だけでちょんと押した。
lines.english: I watched without really watching for a while. At last, without even picking up the remote on the table, I reached out and tapped one of its buttons with a fingertip.

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間、スピーカーから陽気な笑い声がどっと弾けた。
lines.english: The next instant, a burst of cheerful laughter exploded from the speakers.

lines.japanese: 撮影スタジオの舞台裏っぽい風景。いまは三枚目の賑やかしレポーターとして落ちついている元人気アイドルが、いまをときめく十代の役者たちにからかわれて白々しい悲鳴をあげていた。
lines.english: Something resembling the backstage area of a television studio. A former idol, once wildly popular and now comfortably employed as a clownish entertainment reporter, was being teased by the latest crop of teenage actors and letting out transparently false shrieks.

lines.japanese: たまたま選んだ民放局のニュースバラエティは、ちょうど芸能情報のコーナーだったみたい。うん。兄と妹ふたりで迎えるブレックファーストには、こういう明るい番組の方が似合うんじゃないかな。
lines.english: The commercial station I had landed on by chance seemed to be in the entertainment segment of its morning news show. Yes. Surely something this bright was better suited to a breakfast shared by brother and sister.

lines.japanese: 「お、おまたせっ」
lines.english: “S-sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: ふっ、と正面に黒い影がよぎった。
lines.english: A dark shape swept across my vision.

lines.japanese: ことっ。
lines.english: Clink.

lines.japanese: 僕の前にマグカップと白いプレートが置かれる。
lines.english: A mug and a white plate appeared before me.

lines.japanese: トースト、目玉焼き、火を通したベーコンにウインナーソーセージ。パン一枚きりの小鳩の皿よりちょっと賑やかだった。
lines.english: Toast, a fried egg, cooked bacon, and breakfast sausages. It was rather livelier than Kobato’s plate, which held a single piece of bread.

lines.japanese: 「え？　あれ？」
lines.english: “What? Wait.”

lines.japanese: 僕は大げさに首を振って、メニューの異なる自分と妹の食膳とを交互に見比べてみせる。小鳩がそのリアクションの意図に気付いて、首と右手をぶんぶん横に振った。
lines.english: I swung my head theatrically between my breakfast and my sister’s, inviting her to compare the two menus. Kobato caught my meaning and frantically shook both her head and her right hand.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ううん、いいの。私、あの、あんまりおなか空いてないから」
lines.english: “Oh, no, it’s fine. I’m, um… I’m not very hungry.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Oh. Okay.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 小さく顎を沈めて、小鳩は自分の座布団に戻る。
lines.english: Kobato dipped her chin and returned to her cushion.

lines.japanese: 「……きます」
lines.english: “…Thanks for the food.”

lines.japanese: 制服のスカートをきちんと腿の裏に挟んで座り、チベットあたりの修行僧みたいに姿勢正しく手を合わせて食事再開。
lines.english: She tucked the skirt of her uniform neatly beneath her thighs, sat with the faultless posture of a monk from somewhere in Tibet, pressed her palms together, and resumed her meal.

lines.japanese: 「いただきます……」
lines.english: “Thanks for the food…”

lines.japanese: 僕も真似するみたいに短く手を合わせてから、トーストにかぶりついた。
lines.english: I briefly pressed my hands together in imitation of her, then bit into my toast.

lines.japanese: いい焼き具合だ。かりかりした表面ともちもちした内側とで調和が取れてる。パン本来のプレーンな味わいが楽しめた。
lines.english: It was toasted just right, the crisp surface in perfect balance with the soft, springy middle. I could savor the simple taste of the bread itself.

lines.japanese: 「へえー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 飲みこんで、口の中を空にしてから言った。
lines.english: I swallowed and cleared my mouth before speaking.

lines.japanese: 「これ、いいパンでしょ。何も付けなくても美味しいもんね」
lines.english: “This is nice bread, isn’t it? It tastes good even without anything on it.”

lines.japanese: しかし話しかけた相手は、僕と目が合うとまるで何も聞こえなかったかのように無言で立ちあがってしまった。
lines.english: But when the person I had addressed met my eyes, she rose in silence as though she had not heard me at all.

lines.japanese: 白い靴下がすたすたすたと畳を渡る。黒いセーラー服は、ふたたびダイニングへ通じる木枠をくぐって消えた。
lines.english: White socks pattered briskly across the tatami. The black sailor uniform passed once more through the wooden frame into the dining room and vanished.
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese: 僕のぎこちない笑顔は、硬めのヘアスプレーを吹きつけたみたいに固まった。
lines.english: My awkward smile froze in place as though lacquered with extra-hold hairspray.

lines.japanese: 遮るもののなくなった真向かいのガラス戸から、禿げた庭木が悠然と僕を見おろしていた。
lines.english: With nothing left to block the glass doors across from me, the bare garden trees gazed down in serene indifference.

lines.japanese: 「え、えっと……あの、こば……」
lines.english: “Um… Kob—”
“—ato…”

lines.japanese: しかし呼ぶより早く、彼女は席を立ったとき同様なにも言わずに小走りで戻ってきた。
lines.english: Before I could finish calling her, however, she came trotting back, as silent as she had been when she left.

lines.japanese: そして、やっぱりなにも言わずに、マーガリンといちごジャムとメイプルシロップとツナマヨ風味のスプレッドを、ひとつずつコトリ、コトリ、コトリと僕の前に並べていった。
lines.english: Still without a word, she set margarine, strawberry jam, maple syrup, and tuna-mayonnaise spread in a row before me, each landing with its own little clink.

lines.japanese: 肩で息しながら、にへらっとぎこちない笑顔で僕の顔をうかがい、それらの上でてのひらをふたつ広げる。好きなものを塗れ、ということらしい。
lines.english: Breathing hard, she peered at my face with a strained, lopsided smile and spread both palms above her offerings. Apparently I was to help myself to whichever I liked.

lines.japanese: いや、べつに催促したつもりじゃなかったんだけど……でも、まあ。
lines.english: I had not meant to ask for anything… But, well.

lines.japanese: 「ありがと」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 彼女は満足そうに頷いて席に戻る。そして、もう一度ふたりして手を合わせ、今度こそ朝食再開。
lines.english: She nodded in satisfaction and returned to her place. We both pressed our hands together once more, and this time breakfast truly resumed.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、じゃあどれにしようかな、あはは」
lines.english: “Hmm, which one should I choose? Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 僕はおとなしい園児の相手をする保父さんみたいに笑いかけながら……とりあえずマーガリンを選んだ。迷ったときにはいつだって無難な選択を取ろう。食卓は人生の縮図だ。
lines.english: I smiled at her like a nursery-school teacher humoring a quiet child… and settled on margarine. When in doubt, always choose the safe option. The breakfast table was life in miniature.

lines.japanese: かさ……かさ……
lines.english: Scrape… scrape…

lines.japanese: トーストの表面をバターナイフで撫でる乾いた音。
lines.english: The dry sound of a butter knife stroking the surface of toast.

lines.japanese: 兄妹のあいだに会話はない。
lines.english: No words passed between brother and sister.

lines.japanese: なかばタレントみたいな扱いの女性アナウンサーが、コメンテイターの経済学者に小学生みたいな質問を投げかけていた。
lines.english: A female announcer treated almost like a celebrity was asking the economist on the panel questions worthy of a grade-schooler.

lines.japanese: 目玉焼きにナイフを通すと、皿の上でどろりと黄身が広がる。僕は画面の向こうの足立アナを見習って、この際なんでもいいからとりあえず口を開こうと思った。
lines.english: When I cut into the fried egg, the yolk oozed across the plate. I decided to follow the example of Adachi, the announcer on the screen, and simply open my mouth. At this point, anything would do.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: テレビの方、つまり右斜め前を向いていた小鳩の首が、僕の呼びかけで正面に戻る。
lines.english: Kobato had been facing the television, diagonally to her right. At my voice, her head turned to face me.

lines.japanese: じーっ。
lines.english: Stare.

lines.japanese: 真剣な表情で僕の言葉を待っている。
lines.english: She waited for me to continue, her expression perfectly serious.
“Um…”

lines.japanese: 僕はトーストや目玉焼きやベーコンに目を落としながら台詞……言葉を探した。
lines.english: I lowered my eyes to the toast, the fried egg, the bacon, searching for my line… for words.

lines.japanese: 「えっと、さっきの続きなんだけどさ、これって結構いいパンだよね」
lines.english: “So, about what I was saying before. This really is pretty good bread, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 僕は笑顔を作って顔を上げた。
lines.english: I arranged a smile on my face and looked up.

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 小鳩は黒々とした丸い目で真剣に僕を見つめながら、素早く頷いた。
lines.english: Kobato gave a quick nod without taking her grave, round black eyes from mine.

lines.japanese: 「あれかな、やっぱり、パン屋さんのパンってやつ」
lines.english: “Is it what you’d call proper bakery bread?”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 名は体を表すのか、小鳩は公園を歩く鳩みたいによく首を振る子だった。
lines.english: Kobato—“little pigeon”—was true to her name, forever bobbing her head like a pigeon strutting through a park.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱりね、パン屋さん。うん。どこのお店？」
lines.english: “Ah, I thought so. From a bakery. Right. Which one?”

lines.japanese: ちょっと意地悪だったけど、今度はイエス・ノーで答えられない質問を放ってみた。
lines.english: It was a little mean of me, but this time I tried a question she could not answer with yes or no.

lines.japanese: 小鳩はじっと僕を見詰めながら、しばらくもぐもぐと顎を上下させ……やがて首を引っこめる亀のような動きで、こくりと口の中のものを呑みくだした。
lines.english: Kobato held my gaze, her jaw working in silence for a while. At last she swallowed with a little bob, drawing her head back like a turtle retreating into its shell.

lines.japanese: 「──あの、花、花水木通りに新しく出来た」
lines.english: “Um—the new one on Ha… Hanamizuki Street.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あの店。へえ、そうなんだ。いいね。うち、常連になろっか」
lines.english: “Oh, that place. Huh, I see. Nice. Maybe we should become regulars.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……うん」
lines.english: “Yeah… Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 今度の首肯は音声付きだった。しかもダブルで。
lines.english: This time the nod came with sound. Twice, even.

lines.japanese: ところが彼女はそのまま動かない。なお僕を見つめて、パンには手を付けず行儀よく次の言葉を待っているようだった。
lines.english: And yet she did not move. She kept her eyes on me, her bread untouched, waiting with perfect manners for whatever I would say next.

lines.japanese: 僕は焦った。次の言葉、次の言葉……。
lines.english: I began to panic. Something else. I had to say something else…

lines.japanese: 「へー、あの店ねえ」
lines.english: “Huh. That place.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、なるほどねー」
lines.english: “Hmm. I see.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.
“Huh…”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: Nod.

lines.japanese: 僕はグルメ番組のレポーターみたいに、咀嚼してるさまがはっきり分かるよう、もぐもぐと大きく口を動かしながらきつね色のパンを味わった。
lines.english: I savored the golden-brown toast, chewing in broad, conspicuous motions like a reporter on a food show determined to make sure the audience knew he was chewing.

lines.japanese: 背筋良く正座している小鳩は、正面の兄と向きあったまま、しかしたまに子供らしい落ちつきのなさを伴ってちらりちらりとテレビ画面を盗み見していた。
lines.english: Kobato sat formally on her heels with her back perfectly straight, facing her brother across the table. Every so often, however, a child's restlessness got the better of her and her eyes stole toward the television.

lines.japanese: 「あ、観ていいよ、テレビ」
lines.english: “Oh, you can watch it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Okay.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は首を横へ直角に曲げた。
lines.english: Kobato turned her head a precise ninety degrees.

lines.japanese: そのあとＣＭふたつ分ほど画面に見入ってたけど、それでもう飽きてしまったのか、また僕の方に向きなおってきた。
lines.english: She watched with rapt attention for the length of two commercials. Then, either because she had already grown bored or for some other reason, she turned to face me again.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。小鳩も一応は僕の妹だから、話下手ながら会話はしなくちゃっていう気持ちがあるのかもしれない。
lines.english: What was it? Kobato was my sister, after all. Perhaps despite her shyness, she too felt that we ought to have a conversation.

lines.japanese: よし、分かったよ小鳩。お兄ちゃんと一緒に頑張ろう。
lines.english: All right, Kobato. Your big brother understands. We will get through this together.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、でも、ほんと美味しいよね、このパン」
lines.english: “But really, this bread is delicious, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、すごいよ」
lines.english: “It really is something.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm.”
“Ha ha…”
“Yeah…”

lines.japanese: 発展性のない話題を振る兄と、発展性のない反応をする妹。非はどっちにあるんだろう。
lines.english: A brother who chose a subject with nowhere to go, and a sister whose replies took it nowhere. Which of us was to blame?

lines.japanese: 兄妹の無意味な言葉たちが死に絶えると、反動のせいかテレビの音量がやけに大きく聞こえた。
lines.english: When our pointless words died out, the silence they left behind made the television sound preposterously loud.

lines.japanese: テレビ……ああ、そうだテレビだ。
lines.english: The television… Of course. The television.

lines.japanese: 話題の種を提供してもらおうと２７インチのワイド画面に目をやれば、今週の邦楽ヒットチャート・ベスト５なんて特集をやっていた。
lines.english: I looked to the twenty-seven-inch widescreen in search of something to talk about. It was running a feature on this week’s top five Japanese pop hits.

lines.japanese: トップ１に輝いた男性シンガーのＰＶが流れている。エアーズロックの壮大な岩肌に押しつぶされそうな、四肢を広げて歌う日本人。
lines.english: The music video from the number-one male singer was playing. Against the majestic mass of Ayers Rock, a Japanese man stood with his limbs spread wide, looking moments from being crushed beneath it.

lines.japanese: 「あ、御影クリヤ。これ売れてるよね、いい曲だよね」
lines.english: “Oh, Kuriya Mikage. This is selling really well, isn’t it? Great song.”

lines.japanese: ろくに聞いたこともない新譜のＢメロを、とりあえず誉めた。
lines.english: I offered a compliment to the pre-chorus of a new release I had barely heard.

lines.japanese: しかし小鳩が頭を向けたとたん、意地の悪いタイミングで画面がスタジオに切りかわる。
lines.english: But the instant Kobato turned toward it, the screen cut spitefully back to the studio.

lines.japanese: 大袈裟に画面を差した僕の指は、なんだかひどく馬鹿みたいだった。観客のいないタイミング外しなんて、喜劇にさえならない。
lines.english: The finger I had thrust so grandly toward the screen looked profoundly stupid. Missing your cue without an audience did not even rise to the dignity of comedy.

lines.japanese: 「えっ……どれ？　どの曲？」
lines.english: “What…? Which one? What song?”

lines.japanese: 「や、あの……いま流れてた、御影クリヤの新曲……」
lines.english: “Oh, um… the one that was just playing. Kuriya Mikage’s new song…”

lines.japanese: 僕を覗きこんでいた小鳩の黒目が、アナウンサーのふたり並んだテレビ画面へ向かい……一拍置いて……また戻ってきた。
lines.english: Kobato’s black eyes, peering into mine, traveled to the television screen where the two announcers sat side by side… paused for a beat… and returned to me.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、聞いてなかった……」
lines.english: “Sorry. I wasn’t listening…”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか。ははは」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、その曲が？」
lines.english: “What? The song was?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……いや、いい曲だよねって」
lines.english: “Oh… No, I said it was a good song.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩の「うん」は、同意を示す「うん」じゃなくて、話の続きを促す「うん」だった。
lines.english: Kobato’s “yeah” did not mean she agreed. It meant she was waiting for the rest.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……まあ、それだけなんだけど……」
lines.english: “Um… Well, that was all…”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ、うん」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Yeah.”
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese: そして僕の「うん」は、完結の「うん」だった。
lines.english: And my “yeah” meant the conversation was over.

lines.japanese: そもそもよく考えたら、ああいうヴィジュアル系上がりのねっとりした歌声は彼女の趣味と正反対だ。
lines.english: When I stopped to think about it, that syrupy voice from his days as a flamboyant rock singer was the exact opposite of her taste.

lines.japanese: 広がらない。
lines.english: Nothing came of it.

lines.japanese: 広がらないまま会話は収縮し、やがてトーストをかじる音に呑まれて消えた。
lines.english: The conversation contracted without ever expanding, until the sound of teeth biting toast swallowed it whole.

lines.japanese: いいや。
lines.english: Forget it.

lines.japanese: もういい。はやく食べて出かけてしまおう。僕はいつものように無難な結論を出した。そう遠くない未来にいなくなる兄が、いまさら義理の妹と仲良くなったところで意味はない。
lines.english: Enough. I would finish quickly and leave. As usual, I arrived at the safest possible conclusion. There was no point in growing closer to my adoptive sister now, when her brother would be gone in the not-so-distant future.

lines.japanese: それに一応の会話は交わしたわけだから、今日のノルマはもう達成している。僕は黙って口を動かしながらテレビを観ることにした。
lines.english: Besides, we had technically held a conversation. Today’s quota was filled. I resolved to chew in silence and watch television.

lines.japanese: 嘘っぽいセットが組まれたテレビ局のスタジオは、笑顔とおしゃべりで華やいでいる。あれはどこまでが台本なんだろう。
lines.english: The television studio, with its patently artificial set, glittered with smiles and chatter. I wondered how much of it was scripted.

lines.japanese: 芸能人は高給取りってイメージがあるけど、事実だとしてそれも当然だと思う。少なくとも僕には、ワイヤレスマイクよりもバスタードソードの方が扱いやすいだろう。
lines.english: I imagined entertainers were paid handsomely, and if so, it seemed only fair. I, at least, would find a bastard sword easier to wield than a wireless microphone.

lines.japanese: 四辺形の枠の中では、胸の豊かさが際立つモヘアのセーターを着た女性キャスターが、さっきまでとは打って変わって硬い表情になっていた。
lines.english: Within the four-sided frame, a female anchor in a mohair sweater that emphasized the fullness of her chest had traded her earlier smile for a sober expression.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 不意に小鳩が小さな声をあげた。あげたと言うより、思わず漏れたって感じ。
lines.english: A little sound escaped Kobato. It was less something she said than something that slipped out.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 僕もすぐに、妹が驚いた理由に気付いた。
lines.english: I immediately saw what had surprised her.

lines.japanese: スタジオから画面が切りかわった。次に羽田家のテレビが映していたのは、背広姿と路線バスが目立つ朝の繁華街、そのスクランブル交差点だった。
lines.english: The picture changed from the studio. Our television now showed a scramble crossing in a busy morning district, full of suits and city buses.

lines.japanese: 行き交うひとびとの多くが、無関心を装った眠たげな目で、マイクを持った女性レポーター（と画面には映っていないロケスタッフ達）に視点を置いていく。
lines.english: Many of the passersby cast sleepy glances toward the female reporter with the microphone—and the location crew outside the frame—while pretending complete indifference.

lines.japanese: そして横断歩道の先、その向こう岸には、自動車メーカーのＣＭを流す超大型の街頭ディスプレイがそびえていた。
lines.english: Across the crosswalk, on the opposite side, an enormous outdoor screen towered above them, playing a commercial for an automobile manufacturer.

lines.japanese: 「あ、アルバトロスだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. It’s the Albatross…”

lines.japanese: それは若者向けの店舗が詰まった地上８階建てのショッピングビル。駅舎と向かいあう壁面の巨大なハイビジョンは、言わずと知れた大都市・柳木原のランドマークだ。
lines.english: It was an eight-story shopping complex packed with stores for the young. Its enormous high-definition screen, mounted on the wall facing the station, was the best-known landmark in the metropolis of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「これ、生中継だよね。へえ、いま柳木原にテレビ来てるんだ」
lines.english: “This is live, isn’t it? Huh. There’s a television crew in Yanagihara right now.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Mm.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は生返事をしながら、四角い箱へ少し体を向けた。ＢＧＭはなかった。流行りのしゃれた店を紹介するにしてはレポーターの表情が冷たい。なんだろう。
lines.english: Kobato gave the vaguest acknowledgment and turned slightly toward the rectangular box. There was no background music, and the reporter looked too grim to be introducing some fashionable new shop. What was this?

lines.japanese: 気付くのが遅かったせいで、僕は最初に画面を飾ったであろう見出しを逃していた。いったい何の中継だろう。朝の情報番組はエンタメとニュースがごった煮で油断ならない。
lines.english: I had noticed too late and missed whatever headline must have opened the segment. What were they reporting on? Morning shows mixed entertainment and news into the same stew. You could never let your guard down.

lines.japanese: カメラのフレームが、レポーターを置き去りにして繁華街をゆっくり進む。
lines.english: The camera left the reporter behind and began a slow journey through the shopping district.

lines.japanese: アルバトロスに次いで映しだされたのは、花水木通りに並んだ近代的な外観のファッションビル群。そしてその街並を彩る無数のビルボードや電飾看板。
lines.english: After the Albatross came the sleek modern fashion buildings along Hanamizuki Street, followed by the countless billboards and illuminated signs that colored the cityscape.

lines.japanese: 柳木原のメインストリートが、朝の食卓に四角く切りとられていた。毎日見てる風景も、ブラウン管を通すとちょっと感じが違うように思える。
lines.english: A rectangle cut from Yanagihara’s main street now rested on our breakfast table. Seen through a television screen, even the scenery I passed every day felt subtly different.

lines.japanese: 『日曜日の乱闘事件！　いま若者の街に何が！？』
lines.english: SUNDAY BRAWL! WHAT IS HAPPENING IN THE CITY OF YOUTH?

lines.japanese: 画面の右下に小さなテロップが浮かびあがった。電車の中吊り広告にも負けないチープな煽り。
lines.english: A small caption appeared in the lower right of the screen, cheap sensationalism fit for an advertisement dangling inside a commuter train.

lines.japanese: 「乱闘だって」
lines.english: “It says there was a brawl.”
“Mm…”

lines.japanese: 見れば分かることを口に出して読んでみた。小鳩はモニターチェックしてる放送部員みたいに、じっと画面を凝視していた。
lines.english: I had read aloud what anyone could see. Kobato stared intently at the screen like a broadcasting-club member checking the monitor.

lines.japanese: やがて映像は、高層建築の屋上カメラが捕えたような柳木原の俯瞰図に切りかわる。
lines.english: Presently, the picture changed to an overhead view of Yanagihara, seemingly captured by a camera atop a high-rise.

lines.japanese: いくつもの鉄道路線が集束する一大ターミナル駅。そして、その東西南北に広がる背の高い街並。
lines.english: A vast terminal where multiple railway lines converged, with a tall city spreading north, south, east, and west around it.

lines.japanese: 僕も小鳩も毎日、満員の地下鉄に押しこまれて柳木原まで通っている。もちろん今日だって、あと数十分後にはあの中の線路のひとつを通ってるはずだ。
lines.english: Every day, Kobato and I were packed into crowded subway cars and carried to Yanagihara. Today would be no exception. In a matter of minutes, we would be traveling along one of the tracks on that screen.

lines.japanese: 画面がふたたび女性レポーターに戻った。彼女はアルバトロスから先へ進んでいた。
lines.english: The picture returned to the reporter. She had moved on from the Albatross.

lines.japanese: 「えー、ご存知の方も多いと思いますが、いま私が歩いているこちら……この辺りが通称グローヴ街と呼ばれる通りの、中心部になります」
lines.english: “As many of our viewers will know, the area I’m walking through now… this is the heart of the street popularly known as Grove Street.”

lines.japanese: 小走りに近い速度で歩いているせいか、レポーターの息は上がり気味だった。マイクロフォンはそんな雑音を拾いながら、むりやり興奮を抑えたような声を全国に届ける。
lines.english: The reporter was walking at nearly a trot, and her breath came a little short. The microphone gathered that noise as it carried her voice across the country, a voice that seemed to be forcibly suppressing its excitement.

lines.japanese: 「週末ともなれば学生や若者たちでごった返す、この雑然としたショッピング街ですが……ご覧のように、この時間帯はまだほとんどの店が開いておりません。ひとの姿もまばらです」
lines.english: “This disorderly shopping district is packed with students and other young people on weekends. But as you can see, at this hour nearly all the shops remain closed, and there are very few people on the street.”

lines.japanese: 抑揚を制限した低めのトーンが、視聴者の緊張感を適度に煽る。ブラウン管の向こうで暮らすひとびとはみんな話術が巧みだ。
lines.english: Her low, carefully restrained delivery stoked just the right degree of tension in the audience. Everyone who lived beyond the television screen was a master of words.

lines.japanese: 「えー、少年らによる乱闘事件は昨日１２月３日、日曜日の夕方から夜にかけて起こったと見られています」
lines.english: “The brawl involving a group of boys is believed to have occurred yesterday, Sunday, December third, sometime between late afternoon and evening.”

lines.japanese: シャッターが下りた古着屋の前で女性は歩幅を落としてゆき、やがてカメラがその隣りの雑居ビルをフレームに収めたあたりで立ちどまった。
lines.english: The woman slowed in front of a shuttered secondhand clothing store. When the neighboring mixed-use building entered the camera’s frame, she stopped.

lines.japanese: ふたつの建物のあいだには、狭くて暗い不吉な空間が口を開けている。雑居ビルの側面には、金融会社や居酒屋のカラフルな看板が縦一列に張りだしていた。
lines.english: A narrow, dark, ominous space gaped between the two buildings. Colorful signs for a finance company and several drinking places projected in a vertical row from the mixed-use building’s wall.

lines.japanese: 「乱闘事件……？」
lines.english: “A brawl…?”

lines.japanese: 僕はまた繰りかえした。こちらの世界で耳にする血生臭い話は、テレビ越しのせいもあってか、いつもいまひとつピンと来ない。
lines.english: I repeated the words once more. Bloody stories from this world never felt entirely real to me—perhaps partly because I was hearing this one through a television.

lines.japanese: でも考えてみると、にぶく光った段平を構える鎖かたびらのゴブリンより、震える手でカッターナイフを握る学生服の方が何倍も恐ろしく思える。僕にとってはそっちの方がよっぽどファンタジーだ。
lines.english: Yet when I thought about it, a student in uniform clutching a box cutter with a trembling hand seemed many times more frightening than a chain-mailed goblin brandishing a dull-glinting sword. To me, the former was fantasy.

lines.japanese: 「なんだろ、暴走族かな」
lines.english: “What do you think? Biker gangs?”

lines.japanese: 僕は最近聞かなくなって久しい単語を口にしてみた。
lines.english: I tried out a term I had not heard anyone use in years.

lines.japanese: 「わかんない」
lines.english: “I don’t know.”

lines.japanese: いまどきそんなの、って笑ってほしかったのに、小鳩は神妙に首を傾けた。時代に疎い兄貴と思われたかもしれない。
lines.english: I had hoped she would laugh and say nobody had those anymore, but Kobato merely tilted her head in solemn thought. Perhaps she now believed her brother was hopelessly behind the times.

lines.japanese: 「通行人の証言によると、まずこちら、この路地の奥から、罵声や怒号のような声が複数聞こえてきたということで──」
lines.english: “According to witnesses, it began with several voices—shouting and angry abuse—coming from somewhere farther down this alley…”

lines.japanese: 息の整ってきたレポーターが、状況を淡々とこちら側へ伝える。朝の兄妹ごっこを中断させた若い声。
lines.english: Her breathing now under control, the reporter delivered the facts to our side of the screen in an even voice. A young voice that had interrupted our little game of brother-and-sister breakfast.

lines.japanese: 「ご覧いただけますでしょうか。こちらの歩道から、えー、血痕と思われる染みが点々と……路地の向こうへ伸びております」
lines.english: “Can you see this? From the sidewalk here, a trail of what appear to be bloodstains continues at intervals… down into the alley.”

lines.japanese: レンガ色のカラー舗装にまぶされた赤黒い染みが、全国のお茶の間に容赦なくズームアップされた。
lines.english: The camera zoomed mercilessly in on the dark red stains scattered across the brick-colored pavement and carried them into living rooms across the country.

lines.japanese: カメラマンとレポーターが、古い特番の探検隊よろしく雑居ビル脇の路地へ侵入する。
lines.english: Like the expedition team from some old television special, cameraman and reporter ventured into the alley beside the building.

lines.japanese: 「えー、美空署の少年課・地域安全課などによりますと、柳木原では一年ほど前から、暴行・傷害・窃盗、さらには道交法違反、麻薬取締法違反などの罪で検挙される若者の数が増加している一方で──」
lines.english: “According to Misora Police’s juvenile and community-safety divisions, Yanagihara has seen a rising number of young people arrested over the past year for assault, battery, theft, traffic offenses, and even violations of the Narcotics Control Act…”

lines.japanese: 「──地域住民からは、こういった非行少年同士の衝突やいさかいが目立つようになったという不安も寄せられており、警察では事件の調査を進めるとともに、周辺の警戒態勢をより強化する方針だということです」
lines.english: “…while residents have also expressed concern over an increase in clashes and altercations between juvenile delinquents. Police intend to strengthen patrols throughout the area as they continue their investigation.”

lines.japanese: 「なお事件当時、現場付近には数名の不審な若者がたむろしていたとのことで、警察ではその男たちが事件に関与していたものとして足取りを追っています」
lines.english: “Several suspicious young men were reportedly loitering near the scene at the time. Police believe they were involved in the incident and are working to trace their movements.”

lines.japanese: レポーターは握った手を胸のボタンひとつ分落とし、マイクと唇の距離をわずかに開けた。
lines.english: The reporter lowered her microphone hand from one button on her chest to the next, drawing the microphone a little farther from her lips.

lines.japanese: 姿の映っていないスタジオの司会者が、現行の少年法の限界およびその見直しに関してをわずか数秒にまとめてコメントし、次いで女性週刊誌的な観点の疑問をいくつか中継先に投げかけた。
lines.english: The unseen studio host compressed the shortcomings of the current juvenile law and the case for reform into a few seconds of commentary, then lobbed several questions fit for a women’s weekly magazine back to the live report.

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうですね、警察の調べによりますと──」
lines.english: “Yes, that’s right. According to the police investigation…”

lines.japanese: 話しつづけるレポーターの左上、画面隅に貼りついた白い数字が僕のタイムリミットを告げていた。そろそろ席を立って仕度しないと、駅まで走らなければならない時刻だ。
lines.english: In the upper left, above the reporter as she spoke, white numbers fixed to the corner of the screen announced my deadline. If I did not get up and prepare soon, I would have to run to the station.

lines.japanese: 「あー残念。おれ、もう行かないと」
lines.english: “Ah, what a shame. I have to go.”

lines.japanese: 独り言にしては大きい声で僕は告げた。僕の学校は小鳩のところと比べると、家からの所要時間はほぼ同じくらいだけど、始業時間が２０分早い。
lines.english: I announced it in a voice too loud to pass for talking to myself. My school took about as long to reach as Kobato’s, but classes began twenty minutes earlier.

lines.japanese: 「私、もう少し観てから」
lines.english: “I’m going to watch a little longer.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は画面から目を離さないまま答えた。兄はテレビに負けた。
lines.english: Kobato answered without taking her eyes from the screen. Her brother had lost to the television.

lines.japanese: 「うん。じゃ、お先に」
lines.english: “Okay. I’ll be off, then.”

lines.japanese: ごちそうさま、と言って膝を伸ばすと、小鳩は僕を見ずにぼんやりと頷いた。
lines.english: “Thanks for breakfast.” I straightened my knees and rose. Kobato gave an absent nod without looking at me.

lines.japanese: 僕はふたり分の食器を下げて手早く洗った。
lines.english: I cleared both our dishes and washed them quickly.

lines.japanese: 小鳩の目が釘付けなのも当然だ。国内有数の繁華街・柳木原がテレビに映ること自体はそう珍しくもないけれど、刑事事件の舞台として報道されれば誰だって気になるはず。
lines.english: No wonder Kobato could not tear her eyes away. Yanagihara, one of the country’s great shopping districts, appeared on television often enough; but anyone would pay attention when it made the news as the scene of a crime.

lines.japanese: そう、それだ。
lines.english: Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: よし、きょうは学校が終わって帰ってきたら、小鳩に詳しい話を聞こう。
lines.english: All right. When I came home from school today, I would ask Kobato all about it.

lines.japanese: でも……まあ、場合によってはニュースサイトでも覗けばいいや。
lines.english: Though… depending on how things went, I could always check a news site instead.

lines.japanese: 僕は最後の皿を洗い籠に立てると、手にぬるいお湯をすくって顔へ持っていった。
lines.english: I stood the last plate in the drying rack, cupped some lukewarm water in my hands, and brought it to my face.

lines.japanese: なんだか頭が冴えないのは、きっと戦う準備の整っていないテストが待っているからだ。
lines.english: My head felt so dull because an exam I was wholly unprepared to fight was waiting for me. Surely that was all.

lines.japanese: そう、それだ。
lines.english: Yes. That was it.
